title: Zero to One
author: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters
blurb: Zero to One grew out of a class on startups that Peter Thiel taught at Stanford, with notes shaped by his student Blake Masters. Its central claim is that real progress comes from creating new things, going from zero to one, rather than copying what already exists. Thiel challenges common business wisdom. He argues that competition destroys profits, and that great companies aim to become monopolies by owning a small market and then expanding. He urges founders to hunt for important truths that others overlook. He also asks them to treat the future as something you can plan and shape, not leave to chance. Drawing on his experience co-founding PayPal and investing early in Facebook, he explains why a few winners dominate outcomes, and why every business should be able to answer seven hard questions.

lessons.b: Real progress comes from creating something new, which is vertical progress, rather than copying what already works, which is horizontal progress.
Great businesses start by asking what important truth very few people agree with you on, because every new company is built on a hidden secret.
Thiel argues the future is not a lottery, so you should replace vague optimism with concrete, long-term plans you actively work to make real.
issues: scene 7: The plan-path drawing looks broken at the end. The last node is a distorted diamond overlapping the flag pole base, and a stray navy line segment extends down-right past the flag, as if the path overshoots the goal. (fix: End the path exactly at the flag base with a normal circular node like the others. Remove the extra trailing segment and the diamond shape. Keep the flag clear of the node so they don't overlap.)
scene 2: Sub-captions 'CAN BE PLANNED' and 'BLURRY, UNKNOWABLE' render at roughly 16px at 1600 width, below the 18px minimum. (fix: Increase these sub-caption sizes to at least 18-20px.)

scene 4: Secondary captions 'BUILT OVER DECADES' and 'MONEY MOVES AROUND' are tiny, about 16px at 1600 width. (fix: Raise these captions to at least 18-20px. Shorten them or widen the caption area if needed.)

scene 3: Quadrant descriptor text ('PLANS HARD, FEARS FUTURE', 'DRIFTING, EXPECTS DECLINE', etc.) is very small, close to or below 18px. (fix: Bump the descriptor lines to at least 18-20px and tighten the icons so the text fits in each cell.)

scene 0: The 'LOTTERY' and 'BLUEPRINT' labels inside the icons are about 16px at 1600 width, below the 18px minimum. (fix: Increase the label size to at least 18px, or scale up the ticket and blueprint icons.)

lessons.b: Fierce competition drives profits toward zero, while companies with monopoly power, like Google, can capture lasting value and invest in the future.
issues: scene 0: The '$' glyph inside the small amber coin at the centre of the dot ring is about 14px at 1600 width, below the 18px minimum, and hard to read. (fix: Enlarge the coin to at least 64px diameter with a '$' of 28px or more, or drop the glyph and keep a plain amber coin.)

lessons.b: Lasting monopolies come from technology that is far better than alternatives, network effects, economies of scale, and branding, starting by dominating a tiny market, as PayPal did with eBay sellers.
A small number of companies and decisions produce most of the results, so you should focus intensely on the few things that could matter enormously.

lessons.t: Seven Questions Every Startup Must Answer
lessons.b: Thiel ties the book together with seven tests covering engineering, timing, monopoly, people, distribution, durability, and secrets, and he uses failed clean energy companies to show what happens when businesses fail them.
